notes: Draft only. Stays under tmp. Dollar amounts, allocation ratios and sensitivity percentages below are source claims read off captions or nearby prose, not reproductions. No figure was treated as proof of forecast accuracy or optimality.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Cite an external poll as background color for the two-asset question, not as a measured market result.
visualization_observations.summary: Third-party poll poster, captioned as The Street's bitcoin poll of 1,005 U.S. citizens and marked [6]. Visible statements include 38% saying Bitcoin hurts the U.S. dollar, an age split on whether Bitcoin helps the dollar, 80% preferring gold to Bitcoin, and a smaller age split on preferring Bitcoin to gold. The top edge of the poster was cropped in the proxy. None of these percentages is an output of this team's model, and the poster text is excluded from author-language evidence.
visualization_observations.exact_claim_supported: The authors point at an outside poll. The graphic itself supports only the printed poll statements that were visible, not any claim about this portfolio.
visualization_observations.missing_or_unverified: Top of the poster cropped. Poll wording is the publisher's, not the authors'. Section 1.2 nearby says the portfolio 'only contains gold and bitcoin', which drops the cash holding the task requires.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Draw the handoff from a prediction module to a decision module and back to the next period.
visualization_observations.summary: Team diagram captioned 'Overall structure of our model'. Prediction Module feeds Decision Module, which feeds gold and bitcoin icons, then Next Period, with a return arrow back to Prediction. No cash, no fees, no dates, no numbers. Prose around it names PADRRI, X-Prophet with a sliding window, and a 5-day SMA; none of those names is printed on the graphic.
visualization_observations.exact_claim_supported: The authors' own figure shows a two-module loop closed by a next-period return. It does not show accuracy, fees, or the cash state.
visualization_observations.missing_or_unverified: No legend. Cash holding absent. The return arrow has no label saying what quantity travels back.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Quote the cited analyst-in-the-loop schematic that the authors use to motivate Prophet, without adopting it as their own experiment.
visualization_observations.summary: Four rounded boxes in a closed curve: orange 'Modeling', green 'Visually Inspect Forecasts', yellow 'Forecast Evaluation', blue 'Surface Problems'. Arrow order is Visually Inspect Forecasts to Modeling, Modeling to Forecast Evaluation, Forecast Evaluation to Surface Problems, Surface Problems back to Visually Inspect Forecasts. A dash-dot diagonal splits the loop into the printed phrases 'Analysis In The Loop' and 'Automated'. Caption: 'Schematic view of the analyst-in-the-loop approach to forecasting at scale, which best makes use of human and automated tasks. [1]'. The [1] sits in the caption only. No axis, number, fee, date, or metric. Equations (4) and (5) sit below the caption and are not part of the figure. Full diagram confirmed on p07-fig3-full.jpg after a first crop cut the blue box.
visualization_observations.exact_claim_supported: The graphic shows a four-stage loop divided into an analyst side and an automated side. It shows no forecast result. The scale and 'best use' wording belong to the caption and to source [1], not to a measurement in this paper.
visualization_observations.missing_or_unverified: Box text and the diagonal wording are the cited source's. Excluded from author-language counts. Nothing on the graphic ties the loop to gold or bitcoin.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Show where the authors insert the XGBoost term and how the two outputs are drawn as being combined.
visualization_observations.summary: Black outline on white. Top box 'X-Prophet' splits downward into 'Prophet' and 'XGBoost'. Prophet feeds a box 'Confidence level'; XGBoost sends a stem labeled 'w2' into a box 'w1 + w2'; a horizontal arrow labeled 'w1' runs from Confidence level into that same box; 'w1 + w2' then points down to 'final predicted value'. A first, higher crop cut the stems and showed only the top split, so the confidence box, the weights and the final box were confirmed only on p09-fig4-full.jpg. Caption printed as 'Figure 4: The structure of improvement prophet X-Prophet' — 'improvement' is not capitalized and 'prophet' is lowercase. The prose sentence above the figure reads 'The structure of X-Prophet is showed in4.', dropping 'Fig.' No citation mark on the graphic or in the caption; [2] appears only at the end of the preceding paragraph. No axis, fee, date, or error number. Equations (17)-(19) are below this crop and were not on the figure.
visualization_observations.exact_claim_supported: The drawing says X-Prophet is a parent of Prophet and XGBoost, Prophet contributes a confidence level weighted w1, XGBoost contributes w2, and the sum is the final predicted value. It does not say how w1 and w2 are trained, and it shows no error.
visualization_observations.missing_or_unverified: The w2 stem meets the box with no separate arrowhead. No constraint w1+w2=1 is printed on the figure (that constraint is prose and equation text). The combining rule and the overfitting claim live in the paragraph, not in the boxes.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Show the raw price paths and their autocorrelation before any forecast is drawn.
visualization_observations.summary: Four panels. (a) gold price rising from about 1200 to above 2000 over a time index near 0-1200. (b) bitcoin from about 0 to about 60000 over a time index near 0-1750. (c) gold autocorrelation, lag 0 equal to 1 then near 0 out to about lag 30. (d) bitcoin autocorrelation, same shape out to about lag 35. No axis unit on the price panels beyond the visible scale. Caption says (a)-(d) show a 'relatively stable sequence'. The prose names a graph test and a unit root test; no unit-root statistic is printed on the figure. Min-Max equation (23) sits above the figure and is not part of it.
visualization_observations.exact_claim_supported: The panels show an upward gold path, a much larger bitcoin path, and autocorrelation that collapses after lag 0. They do not show a unit-root statistic, and the 'stable sequence' sentence is the caption's, not a number read off the axes.
visualization_observations.missing_or_unverified: No calendar dates on the axes. No test name on the autocorrelation panels. Price readings are eye estimates from the proxy, not digitized values.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Show the randomness-test p-value curves the authors use to argue the series are not pure noise.
visualization_observations.summary: Two panels titled 'Pure Radomness Testing' — 'Randomness' is misspelled on the figure. (a) gold, y from 0 to 0.4, x from 0 to 40, starts above 0.4 and falls to about 0 after lag 5. (b) bitcoin, y from 0 to 0.0025, x from 0 to 40, a spike near 0.0026 around lag 5-6 then near 0. Caption says most p-values are significantly less than 0.05, so the sequences are not pure random and this is 'evidence for the following prediction.' The gold curve's first points sit above 0.05, so 'most' is doing work the caption does not quantify. No axis unit and no test name on the axes; the prose names a Q statistic for large samples and an LB statistic for small samples, neither of which is labeled on the plot.
visualization_observations.exact_claim_supported: Both curves fall toward 0 after the first few lags. The graphic does not name the test, and the early gold points are not below 0.05, so the caption overstates what the axes show.
visualization_observations.missing_or_unverified: Sample size, lag unit, and which statistic produced the p-values are not on the figure. The spike height is an eye reading.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Show one Prophet step decomposed into trend, weekly and yearly components.
visualization_observations.summary: Caption in the text layer is doubled, 'Fig. The visualization' followed by 'Figure 7: The visualization of a single step in our method.' One figure, not two. Dates run 2016-10 to 2019-10. Left panel: black points, a blue line, a blue band, y unlabeled and running roughly 1150-1600, x labeled 'ds'. Right stack: trend roughly 1150-1400; weekly with Sunday high, Monday to Friday flat negative, Saturday high; yearly from January to January with a summer trough. No legend. The prose says Prophet returns confidence intervals and interpretable components; the band is consistent with an interval but nothing on the figure names its level.
visualization_observations.exact_claim_supported: One forecast step is drawn with a band and three component panels over 2016-2019. The figure does not state the interval level, and it does not compare against any other model.
visualization_observations.missing_or_unverified: No legend, so point/line/band colors are undescribed. The y quantity is unlabeled. Component readings are eye estimates.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Contrast a fixed training span with a window that advances one step.
visualization_observations.summary: Schematic, not a data chart. Top row of cells 01-15 labeled Traditional Prediction, with a green bracket and a blue bracket both covering cells 01-05. Bottom row labeled Sliding Window Mechanism, green bracket on 01-05, blue bracket shifted to 02-06. Caption: 'The illustration of the proposed sliding window mechanism of prediction model.' No 90-day value on the graphic; 90 appears only in the prose as the practical window.
visualization_observations.exact_claim_supported: The drawing shows the second bracket moving forward by one cell under the sliding-window label and staying put under the traditional label. It shows no accuracy gain.
visualization_observations.missing_or_unverified: Cell count of 15 is a drawing choice, not the 90-day setting. The prose claim that the window 'significantly outperforms' full-window models has no metric on this figure or the next.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Plot the authors' final gold and bitcoin price forecasts against the actual series.
visualization_observations.summary: Two panels. Left title 'The Gold Price Pridicted with Prophet' — 'Predicted' misspelled — legend Actual in blue and Predicted in orange, y about 1100-2100, x index 0-1200. Right title 'The Bitcoin Price Pridicted with Prophet', same legend, y 0-60000, x 0-1750. Caption: 'The final prediction of the gold and bitcoin price using X-Prophet model.' The panel titles say Prophet and the caption says X-Prophet. No intervals and no error metric on either panel.
visualization_observations.exact_claim_supported: The authors overlay a predicted curve on each actual price curve. The graphic does not say which model produced it, because the title and the caption disagree, and it reports no error.
visualization_observations.missing_or_unverified: No MAE, RMSE, or interval. The model-name conflict is recorded, not resolved. Axis readings are eye estimates.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Show how the reported terminal profit changes with the initial gold-buying ratio.
visualization_observations.summary: Single curve. Y axis 'Profit(10k$)' from about 24 to 28.6, X axis delta(%) from 0 to 100. The peak sits just above delta=0 near 28.5, then the curve declines to about 24 at delta=100. Title 'Variety of profit on last day with respect to ratio of buying gold(δ)'. Caption uses 'radio' where the title uses 'ratio'. No error bars. The reported $285,647 is consistent with a peak near 28.5 times 10k dollars but is not printed as an axis label, so the figure supports the shape and the prose states the dollar.
visualization_observations.exact_claim_supported: Terminal profit, as drawn, is highest at a small gold ratio and falls as that ratio grows. The figure does not print 2%, 98%, or $285,647.
visualization_observations.missing_or_unverified: No marker at the reported optimum. No band. The 28.5 reading is an eye estimate, so it is not used as a reproduction of the dollar figure.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Show the month-to-month holding ratio the authors treat as the risk side of the allocation.
visualization_observations.summary: Single curve. Y 'Ratio of bitcoin held and gold held' from 0 to 20, X 'Month' from 0 to 60. The line sits mostly near 1-3 with spikes near 10, near 12.5, and near 20 around month 53. No cash series, no risk statistic, no calendar dates.
visualization_observations.exact_claim_supported: The drawn ratio is usually low and occasionally spikes by several times. The figure does not define the ratio (bitcoin over gold, or the reverse) and does not show a risk measure.
visualization_observations.missing_or_unverified: Spike heights are eye estimates. No volatility number is printed. The prose uses this plot to talk about balance of return and risk; the plot itself has no risk axis.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Show the terminal-profit surface over the two transaction-cost axes the authors actually scanned.
visualization_observations.summary: 3D surface. Both axes, Gold Transaction Cost and Bitcoin Transaction Cost, run from 0 to 0.0030. Colorbar 'Final Profit' runs from about 274k to about 289k. The slope is mainly along the gold-cost axis: higher profit at the low gold fee, lower profit at the high gold fee, with the bitcoin axis looking flatter. Caption 'Sensitive Analysis on gold and bitcoin transaction.' The scanned range does not include the task's 1% gold fee or 2% bitcoin fee. The prose figures 4.86% and 0.35% cannot be read off the surface.
visualization_observations.exact_claim_supported: Within 0 to 0.0030 on both fees, the drawn profit changes more with the gold fee than with the bitcoin fee. The surface does not cover the official fees and does not display the two percentages.
visualization_observations.missing_or_unverified: Colorbar readings are eye estimates. Whether the strategy was recomputed at each grid point is not on the figure. The prose sentence that bitcoin is more sensitive conflicts with this surface and is left standing for the later warning pass.
